# Energy cap falls in October

The cap on standard household energy tariffs will fall by 3% from 1 October, the Energy Tariff Board announced. It is the first fall in the cap for a year.

What it means for a household depends on how much energy the home uses, so it is hard to put a single number on it. For most members the change will be small, though welcome as the evenings draw in.

The cap limits the price per unit and the standing charge on standard tariffs. It does not cap the total bill, so a colder winter can still mean higher bills even with a lower cap.

If you are on a fixed energy tariff, the change does not affect you until your fix ends.

Sources:
- https://news.example.invalid/energy-tariff-board/press/2026-09-cap-falls (Energy Tariff Board press release)
